evidence.field: 樓 字形、說文、形義通解
evidence.text: The entry records 樓 as 木 + 婁, shows a seal-script example and three manuscript examples, and quotes 說文:「樓，重屋也。从木，婁聲。」It explains the basic sense as a building with two or more stories. The visible evidence does not establish an oracle-bone or bronze form.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 樓

evidence.text: The entry gives later applications: an upper structure on vehicles, ships, or walls; a storey of a building; and premises such as teahouses, taverns, or brothels. It cites 《左傳·宣公十五年》 for 樓車, 《史記·平準書》 for 樓船, 王之渙’s Tang poem for 上一層樓, and曹植’s 《美女篇》 for 青樓. These are cited textual examples; they do not by themselves date the creation of the graph or prove a chronological semantic chain.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 樓

evidence.source: Kotobank, citing 精選版 日本国語大辞典
evidence.text: For the Japanese reading/word 楼, the dictionary dates its first cited example for a high or two-storey building to 続日本紀, Hōki 8, ninth month, 777. This is a Japanese lexical attestation, distinct from evidence for the Chinese graph’s earliest use.
evidence.title: 楼(ロウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.source: Kotobank, citing 精選版 日本国語大辞典
evidence.text: The dictionary cites 和名類聚抄 (about 934) for a high watchtower/lookout sense, and dates a Japanese brothel sense to 雑俳・咲やこの花 (1692). This dates the cited Japanese uses, not the origin of those senses in Chinese.
evidence.title: 楼(ロウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.source: 中國哲學書電子化計劃 (Chinese Text Project)
evidence.field: 樓 entry; Shuowen, Guangyun and character references
evidence.text: The search result reports the seal-script form and quotes 說文’s analysis「樓：重屋也。从木婁聲」; it also gives composition 木 + 婁 and Guangyun material. Opening this result failed with HTTP 403, so these details are treated as search-result leads, not independently inspected page evidence.
evidence.title: 樓 - Chinese Text Project

evidence.text: The accessible text states under 屢:「案：今之婁字本是屢空字，此字後人所加。」This is a transmitted Shuowen statement about the history of 婁, not a description of 樓’s graphic development. I found no direct evidence that 楼’s replacement 婁 → 娄 was a corruption rather than an intentional standard simplification.
evidence.title: 說文解字/08

evidence.text: Exact local row for 婁: Mandarin lóu; Middle Chinese field lju; Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[r]o; gloss “drag, trail (v.).” A search of this file found no 樓 row. Therefore this dataset supports the phonetic component’s listed reconstruction but does not furnish a host reading for a direct Old Chinese comparison; I do not substitute the Zhengzhang reconstruction for it.
evidence.title: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction dataset

evidence.field: 樓 Middle and Old Chinese pronunciation references
evidence.text: The opened entry gives Middle Chinese fanqie 落侯切 and Baxter-style MC luw; it lists Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese /*ɡ·roː/ for 樓. This differs in system from the local Baxter–Sagart row for 婁 (*[r]o), and the local Baxter–Sagart file has no 樓 row. These records make a phonetic analysis plausible but do not establish exact same-system host/component reconstructions from the inspected local dataset.
evidence.title: 樓 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: Local exact rows give 楼 kMandarin lóu (HSK extract row 235) and 樓 kMandarin lóu (full readings file row 98098). Other inspected rows record 楼 kCantonese lau4 (96862) and 樓 kCantonese lau4, kFanqie 落侯, kTang *lou, and kVietnamese lầu (98088–98101). Unihan readings are modern/reference metadata, not evidence of an ancient phonetic relation.
evidence.title: Unicode Unihan record, U+697C

evidence.text: UAX #38 explains that Unihan records readings and other reference properties and that individual ideographs are available through its lookup interface. Direct attempts to open the requested character-specific URLs were inaccessible in this web tool. The local values above are therefore reported with the attempted official click-through URL, while character-specific external verification remains a gap.
evidence.title: UAX #38: Unicode Han Database (Unihan)

evidence.text: The entry explicitly labels 楼 as simplified from 樓 (婁 → 娄). Thus the distinct component form 娄 → 婁 relation for the simplified character is classified as simplified_form, not as an inferred ancestor. This source does not give dated stages for the simplification.
evidence.title: 楼 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The Unicode License v3 page grants broad copying and distribution rights for Unicode data files subject to preserving the copyright and permission notice. UAX #38 identifies Unihan.zip as the source of the database data files. The current character pages could not be opened directly, so this is license evidence for Unihan data generally, not a claim that a local extract is needed. A small extract would add little value here because exact local reading rows can be checked directly and upstream character lookup is intended for interactive access.
evidence.title: unihan-database/LICENSE

evidence.field: 樓 字形、說文、形義通解
evidence.text: The inspected entry labels the displayed archaic form as 小篆 (Small Seal), reports no 金文 (bronze) or 甲骨 (oracle-bone) forms, and shows three 簡帛文字 (manuscript) examples. It quotes 說文:「樓，重屋也。从木，婁聲。」and explains the basic sense as a building with two or more stories. Its cited literary examples include an elevated vehicle, a ship structure, a building storey, and premises such as teahouses or taverns. The examples establish uses cited by the entry, not the date of the graph or a chronological chain among senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 樓

evidence.source: 漢字古今字資料庫（小學堂字形演變）
evidence.text: The official site identifies its database as covering character-form evolution and links separate collections for oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal, and clerical changes. This establishes the database’s intended scope, but did not yield an inspectable character-specific 樓 record or image in this run.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形演變

evidence.field: rights notice for query-interface glyph images and glyph-attribute information
evidence.text: The official rights notice says glyph images at the resolutions obtained through the query interface, and their glyph-attribute information, are released under CC0 1.0 within the limits of law. No specific 楼/樓 image was retrieved from that query interface here.
evidence.title: 小學堂版權聲明

evidence.field: 樓 evolution page rights and displayed record
evidence.text: The opened character-specific page identifies U+6A13 and labels a displayed form 小篆 / 說文, but its footer states that Academia Sinica reserves all rights. I therefore treat it as linked evidence, not as an image asset candidate.
evidence.title: 漢字「樓」：字形演變

gaps: The official character-specific Unihan record URLs for U+697C and U+6A13 were attempted but could not be opened; local readings are reported with the requested official URL as click-through evidence, but are not externally verified character-by-character.

The inspected paleographic source showed seal and manuscript examples but no oracle-bone or bronze form. Earliest attestation of the graph and the exact date of the shown manuscript forms remain unestablished.

Shuowen’s explanation is a historical dictionary account, not independent confirmation of the original graphic structure. No source inspected here establishes an alternative formation or a copying corruption in 楼/樓.

Baxter–Sagart local dataset contains 婁 but no 樓 row. Its 婁 reconstruction cannot alone establish a same-system host/component comparison; Zhengzhang’s host form is a distinct system and should remain separately labeled.

No precise chronology was established for extensions from multistorey building to lookout structures, vehicles/ships, individual building storeys, or commercial establishments. The textual examples show usage but not the semantic transitions between them.

No Unihan extract is recommended: the general Unicode reuse terms permit data copying with notice, but the small extract has limited additional editorial value given the local exact rows and upstream lookup interface.

The Xiaoxuetang rights page confirms CC0 for specific glyph images obtained through its query interface, but I could not retrieve a character-specific 楼/樓 record or image URL from that interface during this run.
CUHK lists a seal-script sample and three manuscript examples, but its linked image requests returned cache-miss errors. I have not proposed those image URLs as usable candidates.

The search results did not establish a relevant Wikimedia Commons image for 樓. No glyph image is proposed because the pages actually inspected did not establish an image with both a relevant identity and reusable provenance. The CUHK entry’s no-oracle-bone/no-bronze display is not evidence that no such forms exist elsewhere.
